externalObservations.contentRead: The provider now reports latest version 7.1.51, changed from the locally archived 7.1.50.2. Its 49-entry versions array contains 7.1.51, 7.1.50.2, and 7.1.50, but no string beginning 7.2.

externalObservations.contentRead: The JSON has 139 keyed entries, including separate Traveler element forms. Its 73,817 bytes are byte-for-byte identical to the locally archived 7.1.50.2 charlist (same SHA-256). No character-by-character data or other categories were fetched for 7.1.51.
externalObservations.limitation: This is a provider listing with form variants, not an independent complete 7.2 V1 roster or a full character, weapon, and artifact snapshot.

conclusions.releasedIdentity: 7.1 remains supported by the indexed official update detail and the previously recorded publisher/storefront observation. The direct official article body was not obtained in this refresh.
conclusions.preview72V1CompleteRoster: unavailable from the limited refreshed sources
conclusions.currentProviderDelta: A new 7.1.51 version label appeared; its charlist is unchanged from 7.1.50.2. This is a candidate for separate future inspection, not evidence of a new game-version mapping.
conclusions.failureLedger: The local last sync is successful. Current public GitHub and Lunaris endpoints returned HTTP 200; historical DNS/403/502 failures in earlier research should not be described as a current broad outage. The current official article direct fetch yielded only an application shell, while the search index exposes a notice snippet. The remaining main blocker is missing authoritative 7.2 V1 identity and version-specific completeness evidence.

conflictsOrUnresolvedQuestions: Provider label 7.1.51 is newer than archived 7.1.50.2, but neither the provider index nor the official notice maps it to 7.2 V1.
Provider timestamp resolves to 2026-10-05T10:00:00Z, later than retrieval; do not infer its semantics.
Official page search index exposes update text while direct HTTP/web open returns only an application shell; complete official article bytes remain uncaptured.
The local independent 7.1 weapon inventory is still classified partial; the new provider charlist cannot close that or establish a full 7.2 V1 inventory.
nextEvidenceStep: Seek a source that explicitly binds an immutable provider revision to 7.2 V1 and states its content scope. If one becomes available, first archive its raw public bytes and revision metadata as an isolated candidate, then compare its version-specific roster with an independent inventory before considering any pointer change.
